problem_disposition.summary: evals/run_evals.py's --live mode needs to detect, per trigger-case prompt, whether the deja-vu skill actually fired inside a headless Claude Code run, without deja-vu building and maintaining a custom log-scraping or reply-text-classification harness.

candidate_comparisons.summary: Claude Code's `--output-format stream-json` flag (documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-usage) is a CLI/runtime capability of the agent host, not a capability of the underlying language model itself -- an earlier draft of this entry mislabeled it as a "model capability"; corrected here. It emits a structured JSON event stream for a headless `claude -p` run, which evals/run_evals.py's skill_invoked_in_stream()/_event_has_deja_vu_skill() functions parse looking for a Skill/skill tool_use event naming deja-vu, instead of classifying free text.
evidence_refs: evals/run_evals.py lines 341-426 (claude_supports_stream_json, skill_invoked_in_stream, _event_has_deja_vu_skill, detect_fired), read directly 2026-09-11

candidate_comparisons.summary: Grepping the plain-text reply for the string "deja-vu" (detect_fired's text-grep branch) as a fallback, selected only when claude_supports_stream_json() finds no "stream-json" substring in `claude --help` output -- not selected on a runtime failure of an actual stream-json run. Weaker signal -- a reply could mention deja-vu without the skill actually having fired, or vice versa -- kept only as a degrade path, not the primary detector.
evidence_refs: evals/run_evals.py lines 341-351 (claude_supports_stream_json) and line 455-456 (use_stream/detection_mode selection), read directly 2026-09-11

uncertainty.residual: this corpus entry read evals/run_evals.py's source and the official Claude Code CLI docs; it did not perform a live headless run to confirm skill_invoked_in_stream() actually detects a real deja-vu Skill tool_use event, and no test in tests/ exercises skill_invoked_in_stream, detect_fired, or claude_supports_stream_json (checked 2026-09-11: no matches). The event schema stream-json emits is an external, unversioned surface Claude Code's own release cadence controls, not deja-vu's, and the module docstring itself flags --live results as directional ("may differ from interactive ones"), not authoritative.
uncertainty.confidence: moderate -- the CLI flag and its documented purpose are confirmed against official docs and the exact source lines that use it, but the detector's actual accuracy against a real run is unverified by this corpus entry, and the whole --live mode is explicitly experimental and excluded from CI

reversibility: high -- --live is an optional, non-CI mode; reverting to the reply-text-grep fallback (or dropping --live entirely) touches nothing outside evals/run_evals.py

route_components.output_boundary: evals/run_evals.py --live mode: a boolean (fired/silent) per trigger case, derived from the headless session's output stream
accepted_obligations: keep the reply-text-grep fallback maintained so detection degrades instead of failing hard when stream-json is unsupported
route_components.residual_uncertainty: no live run was performed to confirm detection accuracy; stream-json's event schema is an external, unversioned surface that can change under a Claude Code upgrade; no test coverage exists for the detection functions themselves
route_components.next_action: add unit tests for skill_invoked_in_stream/_event_has_deja_vu_skill/claude_supports_stream_json against recorded fixture transcripts, and/or run a recorded live probe, before upgrading this entry's evidence_level past source-inspected
